clue.text: Social occasion concluding with a boring set of songs

parts.note: a ball is a formal social occasion with dancing
boring means dull, dry

explanation.surface: A party ends with a tedious medley of tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Balladry is ballads collectively, a body of narrative songs.

clue.text: Only just see with impediment overhead

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overhead sits above the other, so it comes first

parts.note: a bar is an obstacle or impediment
Ely is a cathedral city, so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone can only just see because something blocks the view above.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely is an adverb meaning scarcely, by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: Servant showing inadequacy upset you

parts.note: lack means a shortage, an inadequacy

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so its letters run backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A servant's shortcomings annoy his master.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a footman or servile attendant, a synonym for servant.

clue.text: Prometheus was bound to inspire his writing

definitions.text: Prometheus was bound to inspire his writing

parts.words: Prometheus was bound to inspire his writing
parts.note: read 'Prometheus Bound' as the title of a Greek tragedy, and the clue asks for the playwright who wrote it

explanation.surface: The chained Titan of myth was certain to give some author ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Prometheus Bound is a tragedy traditionally attributed to the Athenian dramatist of the fifth century BC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek tragedian is credited with the play Prometheus Bound, so the myth inspired his writing.

clue.text: Notice air that is mysterious surrounding sister — consequence of cloistered life?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the next piece, enclosing it
mysterious suggests the letters of the words before it are obscured, jumbled

parts.note: a sister in religious orders is a nun

explanation.surface: A strange announcement about a nun hints at what convent life costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysterious' rearranges NOTICE AIR into RECIATION, which 'surrounding' wraps round the sister. 'that is' tempts you towards IE, but here it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving up worldly things is what a life in a cloister entails, hence renouncing as its result.

clue.text: Procession of band at end of street

indicators.note: the band comes at the end, after the street's letters

parts.note: a ring is a band, as of metal

explanation.surface: A marching band goes by at the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A string can be a line or procession of things one after another, like a string of horses.

clue.text: Sort of soil that is hard at foot of slope

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the foot means placed below, so it comes last

parts.note: a tilt is a slope or incline
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Firm earth found at the bottom of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilth is cultivated topsoil, the tilled condition of land.

clue.text: Immature and silly action he perpetrated

indicators.note: silly suggests the words have been made a nonsense of, rearranged

explanation.surface: A childish and foolish thing he did.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun, undeveloped, so not yet mature.

clue.text: Gosh, gain would come with railway gismos!

parts.note: gad is a mild oath, like gosh
to get is to gain

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly admires the gadgets a model railway brings.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is gadgets collectively, and gismos is a word for gadgets.

clue.text: Mouth off about European money, as before refusing to toe the line

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to mouth off is to rant
ecus were the European currency units used before the euro

explanation.surface: A rebel shouts about old euro money and will not conform.
explanation.definitionFit: A recusant historically refused to attend Church of England services, so a nonconformist.

clue.text: Cool or possibly cold — needing to be wrapped in cloth

indicators.note: being wrapped in means the cold piece is enclosed by the cloth

parts.note: plaid is a tartan cloth
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: To keep chilly, wrap yourself in a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and unruffled, as cool does of a temperament.

clue.text: They could spell out danger to the tanks ultimately

definitions.text: They could spell out danger to the tanks ultimately

indicators.note: spell out suggests the letters could be rearranged to form other words
ultimately points to the final letter of the word tanks

explanation.surface: Something whose letters warn armoured vehicles of peril.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of DANGER TO THE plus S, the last of 'tanks', rearrange to the answer. These concrete pyramids were anti-tank obstacles in World War II, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: These rows of concrete blocks were built to stop tanks, so they literally spell danger to them.

clue.text: Shelter by church suits worm

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A churchyard's sheltered spot is good for worms.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a blood-sucking annelid, a kind of worm.

clue.text: Great Scott — he wanted to be as far from there as possible!

definitions.text: Great Scott — he wanted to be as far from there as possible!

parts.words: Great Scott — he wanted to be as far from there as possible!
parts.note: Captain Scott raced for the southern pole, so he wanted to be at the opposite end of the Earth from the northern one

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise, followed by someone longing to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Scott' looks like an exclamation; it is the explorer Robert Falcon Scott, who reached the South Pole in 1912.
explanation.definitionFit: The point at the top of the globe is as far as possible from Scott's southern goal.

clue.text: Someone with a medical career taking off?

definitions.text: Someone with a medical career taking off?

parts.words: Someone with a medical career taking off?
parts.note: 'career taking off' looks like a booming job, but read literally the medic takes off in an aircraft

explanation.surface: A physician whose career is suddenly thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia the airborne medical service flies doctors to patients in remote areas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a doctor who travels by plane to reach patients, so the medical work literally takes off.

clue.text: Alert old boy kept on retainer

indicators.note: in a down clue, kept on means placed above, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: a retainer is a servant of a household

explanation.surface: A watchful veteran retained by his employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice, watchful, just as alert does.

clue.text: Albert, for instance, as the fellow on duty?

definitions.text: Albert, for instance, as the fellow on duty?

parts.words: Albert, for instance, as the fellow on duty?
parts.note: an albert is a kind of chain for a timepiece, so read the clue as a timepiece plus a fellow, someone keeping guard

explanation.surface: A man named Albert is the one working the shift.
explanation.walkthrough: An albert is a watch chain, named after Prince Albert, so the clue hints at a 'watch' and a 'man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard who keeps watch, especially at night, is a person on duty.

clue.text: Be like one relatively inattentive and innocent

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to notice fewer things, as an inattentive person would

explanation.surface: Being a little absent-minded can make someone seem guileless.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without a stain, hence morally pure, and split it means to notice less.

clue.text: Pas is one step — when dancing, that shows relevance!

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters moving about and changing places

explanation.surface: A ballet lesson notes that a pas is a single step.
explanation.definitionFit: Appositeness means aptness, being pertinent, which is relevance.

clue.text: Article seen up tree could be bomb

indicators.note: in a down clue, seen going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a palm is a tree

explanation.surface: Something is spotted up a tree that might be explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied incendiary used in bombs, so here a bomb by metonymy.

clue.text: Worry about good people being led by one of their number

parts.note: a single saint, ST, is one of the good people
re means about, concerning
SS is the abbreviation for saints, good people

explanation.surface: Concern grows about virtuous folk following a leader from among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being led by' says ST comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is anxiety or strain, much the same as worry.

clue.text: Ruthless one has an edge

definitions.meaning: a razor with an open blade has a sharp edge

explanation.surface: A ruthless rival has the advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means merciless, and an open razor of that name has a cutting edge.

clue.text: Report of army stockpile

indicators.note: report means what is heard, a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a horde is a large crowd, an army

explanation.surface: News reaches us of a military supply dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a secret store of valuables or supplies, a stockpile.

clue.text: Meat to get hot and go off when stored

indicators.note: stored means one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: food that goes off rots
as means when, at the time that

explanation.surface: Meat heats up and spoils while kept in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat put in the oven to cook.

clue.text: Frenzied female, demented woman getting caught

indicators.note: the woman is caught, held inside the other piece

parts.note: demented means mad
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wild woman, out of her mind, is arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A maenad was a frenzied female follower of Dionysus, hence any raving woman.

clue.text: Author from American state showing change of character

indicators.note: change of character means one letter swapped for another

parts.note: Delaware is a US state

explanation.surface: A writer from Delaware becomes a different person.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the W of DELAWARE for M.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet and novelist, an author.

clue.text: Inventor suffers setback — time to leave field of activity

definitions.text: time to leave field of activity

indicators.note: a setback sends the word backwards

parts.note: Thomas Edison was the inventor of the phonograph and light bulb

explanation.surface: A failed inventor decides to quit his line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, the referee's call of 'no side' ends the match, when players leave the field.
explanation.definitionFit: No side is the rugby term for the end of the game, time to walk off the pitch.

clue.text: Ancient mother appearing with me in paper

indicators.note: in means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: Thetis was the sea nymph mother of Achilles in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A mythical mother appears with me in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the London daily newspaper, a paper by name.
